---
title: "HTMX fragments"
description: "Render the same partial inside a page and on its own, for HTMX swaps."
---

HTMX swaps a piece of the page with HTML the server returns. Write that piece as a partial,
and you can render it in two places: inside the full page on the first load, and on its own
when HTMX asks for it.

```{python}
#| echo: false
import pathlib, tempfile

folder = pathlib.Path(tempfile.mkdtemp()) / 'templates'
(folder / 'todos').mkdir(parents=True)
(folder / 'todos' / 'list.pt').write_text(
    '<ul id="todos">\n'
    '  <li tal:repeat="todo todos">${todo}</li>\n'
    '</ul>'
)
(folder / 'todos' / 'index.pt').write_text(
    '<h1>Todos</h1>\n'
    '<form hx-post="/todos" hx-target="#todos" hx-swap="outerHTML">\n'
    '  <input name="title"><button>Add</button>\n'
    '</form>\n'
    "${render_partial('todos/list.pt', todos=todos)}"
)
template_folder = str(folder)
```

The fragment, `todos/list.pt`:

```html
<ul id="todos">
  <li tal:repeat="todo todos">${todo}</li>
</ul>
```

The page, `todos/index.pt`, includes it:

```html
<h1>Todos</h1>
<form hx-post="/todos" hx-target="#todos" hx-swap="outerHTML">
  <input name="title"><button>Add</button>
</form>
${render_partial('todos/list.pt', todos=todos)}
```

The views render the page on `GET` and only the fragment on `POST`:

```{python}
import flask

import chameleon_rs
import chameleon_rs.flask as chameleon_flask

app = flask.Flask(__name__)
chameleon_flask.configure(template_folder=template_folder)
todos = ['Write docs']


@app.get('/todos')
@chameleon_flask.template('todos/index.pt')
def index():
    return {'todos': todos}


@app.post('/todos')
def add():
    todos.append(flask.request.form['title'])
    return chameleon_rs.render_partial('todos/list.pt', todos=todos).html_text


client = app.test_client()
print(client.post('/todos', data={'title': 'Ship it'}).text)
```

`chameleon_rs.render_partial()` returns an `HTML` object. Its `html_text` is the markup.
Because the fragment is one template file, the page and the HTMX response can't drift apart.

`chameleon_flask.response('todos/list.pt', todos=todos)` does the same and returns a
`flask.Response`, if you'd rather set a content type or status code.
